original_problem.statement: Erman and Sam, Questions about Boij-Soderberg theory (arXiv:1606.01867), Question 6.1: is every integral point of every pure ray in three variables the Betti table of a finite length module over k[x,y,z] or over the enveloping algebra U(H) of the Heisenberg Lie algebra? Question 6.2 is its analogue in four variables.
original_problem.priority: Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu (arXiv:2605.25259, Theorems 3.7 and 3.8) answer both questions negatively over every field, with (1,2,9,8) on (0,6,20,21) and (1,2,5,6,2) on (0,1,4,5,6). Boocher, Huang and Wolf (arXiv:2512.24320) hold the polynomial-ring half of both examples and the classification of the rays with two generators. The pure modules over U(H) from Kostant's theorem are stated by Erman and Sam and announced by Sam. The obstructions over k[x,y,z] used here are those of Buchsbaum and Eisenbud, Erman, and Boij and Soderberg.
original_problem.prohibited_reframing: No CAOS result may be described as the first negative answer to Question 6.1 or 6.2, as a new obstruction over k[x,y,z], or as a result on the Kostant family. A realization found by a search over a prime field is a statement over that field until it is recomputed over the rationals.

mission: Decide, for the pure rays (0,d1,d2,d3) of small degree, which primitive points are Betti tables of finite length modules over k[x,y,z] and over U(H), with explicit modules and exact computations: the least d3 of a counterexample to Question 6.1, the least realizable multiple on each ray, and how the answers depend on the characteristic of the field.

focuses.title: The realizability table for d3 <= 12 and the least counterexample to Question 6.1
focuses.target: For the 220 pure rays with d3 <= 12: the primitive point realized, excluded or open over k[x,y,z], with the least realizable multiple; the parity-passing excluded rays over U(H); hence the least d3 of a counterexample in characteristic 0.
focuses.value: The published counterexample has d3 = 21; the table shows where the question first fails and separates the two rings. The family U/U(x^e, y^e) and the characteristic 2 statement came out of it.
focuses.success_gate: Every ray with d3 <= 9 decided in characteristic 0 by an explicit module, a cited construction or a cited obstruction, each hit recomputed in a second system (met 2026-11-19: EXP-001, EXP-002, EXP-003).
stop_conditions: A hit on a point excluded by a published obstruction (a bug or a refuted proof): stop and explain.
The search budget of EXP-001 is reached with rays with d3 <= 9 still open.
focuses.novelty_status: Not found in the searches of 2026-11-19 (the literature pass and the two reviews): the modules U/U(x^e, y^e), the dependence of Question 6.1 on the characteristic, a statement of the least d3 of a counterexample. The two rays with d3 = 10 were identified in the programme's dossier of 2026-09-02 from published obstructions. A negative search is not a proof of novelty.

focuses.title: First manuscript: pure resolutions over U(H), the characteristic, and the census
focuses.target: One manuscript with: the family U/U(x^e, y^e) and its sharp characteristic condition with full proofs; the characteristic 2 statement on (0,2,6,8) with its proof; the table over U(H) of the parity-passing rays excluded over k[x,y,z] for d3 <= 12; the census over k[x,y,z] for d3 <= 12; the least d3 of a counterexample in characteristic 0; the methods (exact linear algebra over U(H), the census, the search and its rechecks), the limits and the open rays.
focuses.value: States a characteristic-dependent answer to Question 6.1 on a point that passes the known numerical test, an infinite family of pure modules over U(H) outside the Kostant family, and counterexamples with d3 = 10 against the published d3 = 21, with reproducible exact evidence.
focuses.success_gate: A manuscript at the content bar, every statement traced to a proof or an artifact, read by a reviewer other than the writer with no blocker left, and published on Zenodo with its record metadata (met 2026-11-20: v0.01, 10.5281/zenodo.24385387).
stop_conditions: The review of the least-counterexample statement finds a failing case: the statement is narrowed to what holds before any text claims it.
A source is found that already contains the family, the characteristic dependence or the least counterexample: the manuscript cites it and keeps only what remains.
Two review rounds leave a blocker open: stop and bring the blocker to the next strategic review.
focuses.novelty_status: As in BSR-F1; the manuscript states the searches made and claims no priority.
focuses.first_bounded_action: Done: the reviews of the three derivations and of the lift lemma, the writing, the review with its fix passes and the release. Next: the strategic review that names the following focus (BSR-F3 is proposed).
focuses.review_2026_11_20: Success gate met on 2026-11-20 (v0.01 published, 10.5281/zenodo.24385387). Strategic review of the same day, made under the standing instruction to choose and advance the case with the best prospects: the focus closes and BSR-F3 becomes current.

focuses.title: The characteristic questions left open by the first manuscript, and the open rays
focuses.target: (1) The machine checks of the characteristic 2 theorem and of the family at e = 6, 7 archived with the repository's instrument (EXP-005). (2) The point (1,2,2,1) on (0, e, 3e, 4e) in odd characteristic below 2e, for e = 3 and 4: a pure pair of forms over GF(p), or a recorded negative with its method (EXP-006). (3) The 15 rays with d3 >= 10 whose primitive point is open over k[x,y,z]. (4) The substitution of x^e, y^e in the Kostant presentations.
focuses.value: Item (2) decides whether characteristic 2 is the only characteristic in which the point fails for small e, and whether the family U/U(x^e, y^e) is part of a larger family of pure modules (the locus of the rank condition has dimension at least 12 in a Grassmannian of dimension 14 at e = 4, by a Thom-Porteous class computed before the run). Item (1) gives the manuscript an artifact for each machine claim.
focuses.success_gate: EXP-005 confirmed with its four gates; for e = 3 and e = 4 and every odd prime below 2e, either a pure pair confirmed in a second system or a recorded negative with its method; the outcome reviewed by a reader other than the writer before the manuscript states it (v0.02). Met 2026-11-20: v0.02 published (10.5281/zenodo.24388904) after a review by a reader other than the writer with a fix pass, a closing check and a final confirmation.
stop_conditions: A finite length module with at most one more relation than generators in characteristic 2 (a defect or a refuted proof): stop and examine before anything else.
Three consecutive experiments decide no characteristic question and no ray.
A source is found that already contains the statement on odd characteristic: cite it and keep only what remains.
focuses.novelty_status: Open questions of this programme, stated in the limits section of the manuscript v0.01. Not searched as such beyond the literature pass of 2026-11-19; a search is due before any claim.
focuses.first_bounded_action: Done: EXP-005 to EXP-020; ten derivations reviewed after v0.02 (weight classes, central pairs, the criterion, endomorphisms, pull-back, pairs over the invariants, one congruence, the weight-zero projection, the pairs with exponent t, the explicit short pairs); the manuscript v0.03 reviewed by a reader other than the writer and published (10.5281/zenodo.24404456). Next: the strategic review that closes this focus or renews it on BSB-037 and BSB-038.
focuses.review_2026_11_20: The point (1,2,2,1) of (0, e, 3e, 4e) is realized over U in every characteristic other than 2 for e = 2, 3, 4, 5 (explicit pairs, two instruments, rebuilt by the coordinating session; Theorems A and C); at e = 6 it is realized in characteristic 3 and open in 5, 7, 11. The pure pairs form a family of dimension at least 4e - 4 through <x^e, y^e>, exactly 4e - 4 there over the rationals for e = 4 to 7, with an explicit four-parameter linear family for every e >= 4. The manuscript v0.02 was read by a reviewer other than the writer; the success gate is met once it is released.
focuses.review_2026_11_20_exp009: EXP-009 (after v0.02): the linear family contains pure members below 2e at (4,5), (4,7), (5,7), (6,11), (7,11), (7,13), so the point (1,2,2,1) is realized at e = 6 in every characteristic other than 2, 5, 7 and at e = 7 in every characteristic other than 2, 3, 5, 7. Not in the manuscript: it goes into the next version, with a decided open characteristic if one is decided.
focuses.review_2026_11_20_theorems: After v0.02: (1) in characteristic p >= 3, pairs of forms with central coefficients, f = A + beta_1 x + beta_2 y, have a central commutator and are pure exactly when z D, n(f), n(g) have no common zero but the origin; explicit pure pairs for every e >= 3 with e = 0 or 1 modulo p (reviewed; EXP-011 and EXP-012, two instruments, e up to 15). (2) Such a pair makes U free over the image of an endomorphism, and the pull-back multiplies the degrees of every Betti table by d, so the set of realized e in characteristic p is closed under multiplication by d = 0 or 1 modulo p (reviewed; EXP-013). The mechanism exists only for a central commutator, hence only for p dividing d(d - 1), and never in characteristic 0. (3) A necessary condition for pure pairs homogeneous for the weight modulo m, tested on 410 strata (reviewed; EXP-010). (4) EXP-010 finds pure pairs at (6,5), (6,7), (7,3), (7,5); with (7,7) from the central pairs, every pair (e, p) with 2 <= e <= 7 and p odd has an explicit pure pair: the point (1,2,2,1) of (0, e, 3e, 4e) fails only in characteristic 2 for 2 <= e <= 7. (5) For even e the pairs (x^e + b y^e, G(xy, z)) decompose over k[xy, z]; a pure pair over the rationals at e = 4 with second form (xy)^2 - (xy) z + 9 z^2 (reviewed).
focuses.review_2026_11_20_strata: After the theorems: EXP-010 (weight-class strata) settles (6,5), (6,7), (7,3), (7,5), (7,7); EXP-014 settles e = 8 and finds pure pairs (x^e + b y^e, G(xy, z)) at e = 10, 12; a reviewed note shows that for those pairs, under a coprimality hypothesis, one congruence decides the pure Hilbert function and gives the pure Betti table, with existence over a finite field of characteristic p >= 2e - 1; EXP-016 lists the forms by that congruence and settles e = 10 and e = 12; a reviewed note (the projection on the weight-zero summand) proves that the linear family has no pure member for p <= 2e - 5 and excludes strata; EXP-015 confirms the rule of the linear family in twelve more pairs and settles e = 9; EXP-017 finds pure pairs at (11,7) and (13,5) through a filter of two congruences for the odd-e stratum, which is observed and not proved. EXP-018 finds pure pairs at (11,13), (11,17), (13,17), (13,19), (14,23) in the stratum with the largest exponent t the weight-zero bound allows. State: for 2 <= e <= 10 and e = 12 the point (1,2,2,1) of (0, e, 3e, 4e) has a pure pair over GF(p) for every odd prime p below 2e; open at e = 11 (p = 3), e = 13 (7, 11), e = 14 (5, 11).
focuses.review_2026_11_20_exponent_t: Later on 2026-11-20. Two derivations, each read by a reviewer other than the writer (correct, minor repairs): (1) for the pairs x^e + alpha(xy, z) y^t, y^e + beta(xy, z) x^t the module splits over k[xy, z] into 2t + 1 cyclic summands and e - t - 1 summands on two generators governed by one form Delta; under two congruences and a scalar that does not vanish it has length e^3 and the pure Hilbert function when p = 0 or p >= 2t, and it is a pure pair when moreover Delta has no common factor with A_(e-t) (the socle); so the filter of EXP-017 and EXP-019 is a sufficient condition. (2) In the linear family the short pair with ab = 2 is pure for every prime p = 2e - 1 other than 11 and 43 (other short pairs work there), and the short pair with ab = -1/4 for every prime p = 2e - 3 whose Fermat quotient of 2 is not 1/2 or 3/2 (below 2,000,000 the exceptions are 5, 30577, 45827, where other short pairs work): for every prime p >= 5 the point with e = (p + 1)/2 is realized over GF(p), and for every prime 5 <= p <= 2,000,000 the point with e = (p + 3)/2. EXP-019 (the filter for every exponent, random members): pure pairs at (13,11), (13,7), (14,5), (15,19), (15,23), (15,29), (16,23), (16,29), (16,31). EXP-020 (the members fixed by the exchange of x and y, complete lists): pure pairs at (14,11), (15,11), (15,13), (15,17), (16,17), (16,19). State: every pair (e, p) with e <= 16 and p an odd prime below 2e is settled except (11, 3); for 2 <= e <= 16 with e not 11 the point (1,2,2,1) of (0, e, 3e, 4e) fails only in characteristic 2.

manuscripts.split_action: No split: one central question (which primitive points of the pure rays of small degree are Betti tables of finite length modules over k[x,y,z] and over the Heisenberg enveloping algebra, and how the answer depends on the characteristic). v0.02 (2026-11-20) adds odd characteristic below 2e (EXP-006, EXP-008), the locus of pure pairs with its exact dimension at the power pair and the linear family (the two reviewed notes, EXP-007), the archived machine checks (EXP-005) and the correction of the manifest table. v0.03 (2026-11-20) adds the criterion for pairs with a central commutator and its explicit pure pairs, the scaling of Betti tables by pull-back, the weight classes, the decomposition over k[xy, z] with one congruence, the weight-zero projection, the pairs with exponent t (coprimality conditions, two congruences and a scalar give the pure Hilbert function, and a pure pair under one more coprimality), the explicit short pairs for p = 2e - 1 and p = 2e - 3, EXP-009 to EXP-020, and the state of the characteristic question (e <= 16 settled except (11, 3)). No split: the same central question. A new version for corrections, for (11, 3), for the Betti table when Delta and A_(e-t) have a common factor, or for a decided open ray.
